title: Where does the nth appearance of each design sit?
description: A saree border repeats three designs in a fixed order. The position of the nth appearance of each design is found as an expression in n, and the first three positions are listed.
teaching_notes: One idea: in a border that repeats every three places, the nth appearance of the last design is at three n, and the others sit just before it. Watch for students who add three to n instead of multiplying n by three.

source: The border repeats A, B, C. Write the position of the nth ap
video_script.why: A learner sees how a repeating border gives the position of the nth appearance of each design as an expression in n.
video_script.substitution: the book's saree border that repeats the designs A, B and C, with the nth appearance of each design
video_script.anchor: the saree border of the book that repeats three designs in a fixed order
video_script.wrong_answer: the nth C is at n plus three
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the nth C is at n plus three because the border repeats every three places. For n as two, that gives five, but the second C is at six, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: Design C is at three n. Design B is at three n minus one, and design eigh is at three n minus two.

final_answer.value: C at 3n, B at 3n − 1, A at 3n − 2
final_answer.spoken: C at three n, B at three n minus one, and eigh at three n minus two

maths_rules: the border repeats A, B, C with A at 1, B at 2, C at 3
C first appears at 3, 6, 9, so the nth C is at 3n
B is one place before C, so the nth B is at 3n - 1: for n = 1, 2, 3 the positions are 2, 5, 8
A is two places before C, so the nth A is at 3n - 2: for n = 1, 2, 3 the positions are 1, 4, 7
for n = 1, 2, 3 the C positions are 3, 6, 9
check with n = 1: 3n = 3, 3n - 1 = 2, 3n - 2 = 1 match the start of the border
Keeko test: n + 3 gives 4 for n = 1, which is design A, and 5 for n = 2, but the second C is at 6
video_script.design: The border stays on the board; the positions of design C are found first, and the other two designs are found by moving back one and two places.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a saree border with designs A, B, C repeating, positions 1 to 9 numbered

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the saree border is drawn
marks.order: designs A, B, C appear at positions 1, 2, 3 and the order repeats

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book. Someone is weaving a saree border that repeats three designs.
<bookmark mark='order'/>Design eigh is at position one, design B is at two, and design C is at three. Then the order repeats.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Where does the nth appearance of design C sit?

beats.on_screen: the border stays on the board
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the designs repeat in the same order; the count of appearances is n; the nth appearance is the first, second, third and so on

marks.repeat: the three designs are shown repeating again and again
marks.count: the appearances of design C are counted 1, 2, 3 and n
marks.place: the position of each design is numbered from the start

narration: <bookmark mark='repeat'/>The three designs repeat in the same order, again and again.
<bookmark mark='count'/>We call the count of appearances n. The nth appearance is the first, second, third and so on.
<bookmark mark='place'/>The position of a design is its place counted from the start.

beats.on_screen: Given: the border repeats A, B, C
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the border repeats the designs eigh, B and C in this order.

beats.on_screen: To find: the position of the nth appearance of C, B and A, and the first three positions of each

marks.find: the words nth appearance and first three positions are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the position of the nth appearance of each design, and list the first three.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: C appears at 3, 6, 9, ... the nth C is at 3n

marks.list: the positions 3, 6 and 9 are lit under design C
marks.nth: 3n is written beside the nth design C

narration: <bookmark mark='list'/>Step one, design C first appears at positions three, six and nine.
<bookmark mark='nth'/>These are the multiples of three, so the nth design C is at three n.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: B is one place before C, so the nth B is at 3n − 1: for n = 1, 2, 3 the positions are 2, 5, 8

marks.back: an arrow moves one place back from each design C to design B

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step two, design B sits one place before design C.
<bookmark mark='nth'/>The nth design B is at three n minus one, giving two, five and eight.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: A is two places before C, so the nth A is at 3n − 2: for n = 1, 2, 3 the positions are 1, 4, 7

marks.back: an arrow moves two places back from each design C to design A

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step three, design eigh sits two places before design C.
<bookmark mark='nth'/>The nth design eigh is at three n minus two, giving one, four and seven.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check with n = 1: 3n = 3, 3n − 1 = 2, 3n − 2 = 1, which are C, B and A at the start of the border

marks.one: 1 replaces n in the three expressions
marks.match: 3, 2 and 1 are matched with C, B and A at the start of the border

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step four, check with n as one. The three expressions give three, two and one.
<bookmark mark='match'/>These are design C, design B and design eigh at the start of the border.

beats.on_screen: Answer: C at 3n, B at 3n − 1, A at 3n − 2
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Design C is at three n. Design B is at three n minus one, and design eigh is at three n minus two.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the border
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: the nth C is at n + 3, struck out; n = 2 gives 5, but the second C is at 6

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows the nth C is at n + 3
marks.gap: 5 and the position 6 of the second C appear side by side and do not match
marks.fix: the bubble is struck out and 3n is written

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the nth C is at n plus three, as the border repeats every three places.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Try n as two, where two plus three is five.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>But the second C is at position six, not five.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Each new C comes three places later, so we multiply n by three.
